items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: Coleman Hawkins was like his sainted father. I saw him hit a man at the bar one night because he was making fun of the buzz in Coleman Hawkins' sound... it was just one of the most thrilling experiences in my life to hear that man.

ctx.x: So we struck up a friendship then that lasted, I guess, until he died -- until he went to Europe; I didn't see him after that. We met there every night. And Ben was -- Coleman Hawkins was like his sainted father. I saw him hit a man at the bar one night because he was making fun of the buzz in Coleman Hawkins' sound because Coleman Hawkins, you know, had this great style before he went. He came back from Europe and he had a totally different style from when he left. He had that mrrr, and growl and fire and…
on the back. And he would -- physically, one night he got into a fight with a guy who made fun of Coleman Hawkins.
